summary:
Our project, "Places in Türkiye That Resemble Mars and the Moon," is an educational exploration game developed using Scratch by the Cyber Work team.

NASA studies environments on Earth that share characteristics with Mars and the Moon to better understand other worlds. Inspired by this research, we created a game that introduces remarkable natural landscapes in Türkiye, including locations in Burdur, Manisa, Nevşehir, Konya, and Erzurum.

Our game helps address the challenge of making space science understandable and engaging for younger students. Players explore different landscapes, answer multiple-choice questions, and discover connections between Earth's natural formations and planetary exploration.

The project is designed primarily for children aged 10–12. Its short explanations, colorful visuals, and interactive questions make scientific learning accessible and enjoyable.

Our goal is to increase curiosity about astronomy, geography, and nature while showing that the journey to understanding other planets can begin right here on Earth.
details:
Project Details

What does our project do?

Our project is an interactive educational game that introduces natural areas in Türkiye resembling landscapes on Mars and the Moon.

Through this game, children discover fascinating geological formations and learn how studying Earth can help scientists understand other planets.

How does it work?

We developed our game using Scratch, a block-based programming platform.

Players begin their journey on a space-themed introduction screen. As they progress, they encounter different locations in Türkiye and answer multiple-choice questions.

Players select their answers by clicking interactive buttons. The game provides feedback and continues the exploration, helping students learn through participation.

What are the benefits?

Our project helps children:

  • Discover remarkable natural landscapes in Türkiye.
  • Understand connections between Earth and space exploration.
  • Develop curiosity about astronomy, geography, and science.
  • Learn through interactive questions rather than memorization.
  • Explore scientific topics using simple and understandable explanations.

What impact do we hope to achieve?

We want to encourage children to become curious researchers who ask questions about Earth and the universe.

We also hope to demonstrate that scientific exploration does not always require traveling far away. Interesting connections to space science can be found in our own country.

What technologies did we use?

We used Scratch to develop the interactive game.

Scratch's visual programming blocks allowed us to create buttons, questions, answer selections, feedback messages, and transitions between different scenes.

We also used digital illustrations, background images, and presentation slides to communicate our ideas.

The project was developed as a digital educational experience for children aged 10–12.

What makes our project creative?

Our project combines space exploration, geography, and game-based learning.

Instead of focusing only on distant planets, we introduce landscapes in Türkiye that visually resemble extraterrestrial environments.

By presenting these places through an interactive Scratch game, we make the topic more interesting and accessible to younger learners.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team focused on the age of our target audience, ease of use, understandable language, engaging visuals, and educational value.

We designed the project around short explanations and simple multiple-choice interactions so that children could participate without requiring advanced scientific knowledge.
